category: realtime pub/sub messaging over WebSocket and REST

free_tier.stated: Free package: 6,000,000 messages a month, 500 messages a second, 200 concurrent connections and 200 concurrent channels, no credit card and no time limit
free_tier.notes: A message counts on publish and on each delivery: a publish received by 10 subscribers counts as 11, and history reads and integrations count too. The account is also held to 250,000 messages an hour, 50 messages a second per channel and 25,000 HTTP API requests an hour at 50 a second. Count-based limits (connections, channels) refuse new resources until existing ones close; a publish above a rate limit is rejected with an error code. Email notifications go out near and past a limit.

per_object_cap.stated: 64 KiB per published message on the Free package

retention.stated: Message and presence history retrievable for 24 hours by default and 1 day at most on Free; messages in an Ably queue are kept 24 hours
retention.notes: Paid packages raise the history ceiling to 30 or 365 days.

egress.terms: Message bandwidth on Free is capped at 28.6 GiB a month and 1.2 GiB an hour; paid packages charge USD 0.25 per GiB above an allowance of 5 KiB times the messages consumed
egress.free_allowance: 28.6 GiB of message bandwidth a month, 1.2 GiB an hour

interface_detail: REST API at https://main.realtime.ably.net for publish, history, presence, tokens and stats, in JSON or MessagePack; long-lived realtime connections through the Ably SDKs, which the interface vocabulary has no WebSocket term for. The /time endpoint answered 200 without a key.
tooling: Ably SDKs for JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, .NET, iOS and Android, or any HTTP client against the REST API with an API key or token.
chaining: A fan-out layer that pushes job status from free compute workers to browsers or other workers, with one day of history for a consumer that reconnects.

limits.value: 250,000 messages per hour and 500 messages per second across the account
25,000 HTTP API requests per hour, 50 per second
28.6 GiB of message bandwidth per month, 1.2 GiB per hour

limits_note: 200 concurrent connections, 200 concurrent channels and 50 messages a second per channel. The vocabulary has no kind for a concurrency cap.
binding_note: 6,000,000 a month is 200,000 a day (6,000,000 / 30) and every delivery counts, so a fan-out meets the monthly count first; messages that average above 5 KiB meet the 28.6 GiB monthly bandwidth before it (6,000,000 x 5 KiB = 28.6 GiB).

identity_cost.detail: The signup form asks for a full name, an optional company name, an email and a password, or a GitHub or Google sign-in; the Free package needs no credit card.

reliability_note: Rate-limit excess is rejected with an error and count limits refuse new connections or channels; Free support is a best-effort service level objective.
confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from the first-party limits and pricing pages; the REST host was probed and its /time endpoint answered 200 without a key. No message was published, because publishing needs an account key. A publish and history read with a Free key would move it to measured.
